---
title: "Live Pulse-Shape Discrimination"
format: gfm
---

The per-channel **PSD** workspace separates event populations using the two
charge estimates transported in MCA list-mode records. It is a live analysis
view fed by the MCA DMA worker; it does not own another hardware buffer and
does not alter a simultaneously recorded raw event stream.

The displayed ratio is:

```text
PSD ratio = (Qlong - Qshort) / Qlong
          = 1 - charge_energy / trapezoid_energy
```

`trapezoid_energy` is also the horizontal coordinate. Both quantities are raw
producer values until the detector response and event-field interpretation
have been validated for the specific setup.

## CH0 live workflow on `.135`

The following reference run used channel 0 of
`192.168.10.135:30431`. A CAEN generator supplied artificial Na-22 test
signals; this is a functional acquisition example, not a radioactive-source
measurement. No PSU setting was applied or required.

### 1. Run Scope Auto Setup

1. Open **Scope** and select **CH0**.
2. Stop ordinary Scope acquisition and disable **Record DMA frames**.
3. Click **Auto Setup** and wait for the result instead of changing Scope
   controls while its worker is active.
4. Confirm that a real pulse crosses the selected trigger and that the status
   reports *verified*.

In this run Auto Setup found a negative pulse, selected **Falling edge**, set
the DAC baseline to `252`, and set the raw Scope threshold to `28322`.

![Live CH0 Scope after a verified Auto Setup on the `.135` generator
signal.](images/psd-ch0-scope-auto-setup-live.png)

These Scope values describe the Scope ADC path. They are not the MCA trigger
level below and should not be copied between the two signal paths.

### 2. Configure MCA charge comparison

Stop Scope before moving to MCA. Apply these CH0 settings while MCA list-mode
DMA is stopped:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Polarity | Negative |
| Baseline | 64 ns |
| Debug 1 / Debug 2 | Input signal / Trigger signal |
| Pile-ups | 0 |
| Binning | 128 |
| Trigger level | `-512` raw |
| Window length | 1024 ns |
| Pretrigger offset | 24 ns |
| Trigger source | Threshold |
| Charge Comparison | Enabled, 150 ns |
| PSD Zero Crossing | Disabled |
| Zero Crossing mode/window | Mode 0, 8–16 ns (inactive while disabled) |

Charge Comparison is the feature that supplies `charge_energy` for this live
PSD ratio. The separately named **PSD Zero Crossing** block produces timing
markers for another analysis path; it is deliberately disabled in this
example.

![Live CH0 MCA settings and spectrum used for the PSD
measurement.](images/psd-ch0-mca-settings-live.png)

Select **Online only** under **Settings -> General Settings...** when no raw file is
required, then enable **Record list-mode DMA**. Choose Binary, HDF5, or ROOT
instead when the same events must also be retained for offline analysis.

### 3. Configure and acquire the PSD view

Use these client-side display settings:

| PSD control | Value |
|---|---|
| Energy display bins | 1024 |
| Ratio display bins | 256 |
| Energy shift | 0 bits |
| Ratio range | `-1.0…1.0` |
| PSD cut | `0.5344` |

Return to MCA and press **Start**. The PSD workspace begins accumulating only
when MCA list-mode DMA is active and Charge Comparison is enabled. Stop the
MCA measurement and wait for the final drain before treating the matrix as a
completed result.

![Completed live CH0 PSD matrix showing two separated generator populations,
the fitted components, and the FOM quality warning.](images/psd-ch0-live.png)

## Reading the plots

- The left image is a logarithmically coloured energy-versus-ratio matrix.
  Its axes remain raw values.
- The red horizontal line is the movable PSD cut. It classifies the display;
  it does not reject records from a saved DMA stream.
- The blue vertical region selects the energy interval used by the ratio
  projection at upper right.
- The lower plot contains separate raw-energy projections for events below
  and above the cut.

This live run produced two clear fitted ratio centroids near `0.04859` and
`0.72593`. The cut at `0.5344` separates their displayed energy projections.
They are generator populations and are intentionally not labelled as particle
species. Such a label requires detector data from a controlled, independently
identified source and detector-specific validation.

Energy positions, ratio centres, and the best cut depend on detector gain,
pulse shaping, integration time, and source geometry. Repeat the optimization
instead of copying `0.5344` to another channel or setup.

## FOM fitting and gate optimization

The live and offline ratio projections provide a shaded fit ROI and two
draggable centroid seeds. **Fit double Gaussian** performs a bounded
constant-background fit with Poisson-deviance residuals and reports both
centroids and FWHMs, reduced deviance, and
`FOM = |mu2 - mu1| / (FWHM1 + FWHM2)`. Inspect convergence, covariance,
parameter bounds, population separation, and residuals before treating the FOM
as qualified. **Copy table** exports the fitted populations and diagnostics.

For the artificial signal shown above, the fit returned FWHM values `0.05892`
and `0.01460` and a nominal FOM of `9.213`, but its reduced Poisson deviance was
`236`. The visible poor-convergence warning therefore takes precedence: this
large FOM is useful for exercising the workflow, not as a qualified detector
performance result.

In **Waveform Analysis Workbench**, a completed fit can seed **Optimize gates**.
The bounded local search varies the short- and long-gate endpoints while
holding the baseline, integration start, energy/fit ROIs, and centroid seeds
fixed; poor-convergence candidates are rejected. The selected gates are
rebuilt and refitted on the full selected dataset. They are specific to that
detector, source, waveform sample period, and analysis constraints.

PSD Event Readback and Waveform Analysis can download non-overwriting report
bundles containing the matrix, projections, separated spectra, fit components,
diagnostics, settings, provenance, and machine-readable metadata. Waveform
reports also retain the exact gates. See [Analysis Tools](analysis_tools).

## Integrity of the reference run

The final CH0 run transported 304,128 records in 297 complete frames. The MCA
view reported verified continuity with zero DMA faults, zero DMA errors, and
zero list dead time. Of those records, 303,693 entered the displayed ratio
range; 394 had zero total energy and 41 lay outside the configured view. The
PSD subscriber reported zero display-buffer drops.

A visually clean matrix is not enough to establish integrity. Always inspect
the final MCA DMA summary after Stop. A nonzero `list_deadtime_raw`, frame
count mismatch, DMA fault, or display drop makes the affected interpretation
incomplete.

For saved-event reconstruction and bounded offline analysis, see [MCA
List-Mode Analysis](analyze_listmode). For buffer ownership and output modes,
see [Acquisition Workflows](acquisition_workflows) and [Capture Files and
Integrity](data_formats).
